rationale: C1 is in Time order but unrelated to the triage key, so it behaves like a random permutation for ranking. Insertion sort is quadratic; custom quick/merge/heap sorts are n log n. Revised hardened sort has a depth-limited heap fallback.

C2 is a uniformly shuffled total order. Comparison sorts have n log n behaviour; insertion sort is quadratic with a larger constant. Median-of-three should avoid poor pivots. Revised hardened sort has a depth-limited heap fallback.

C3 is already triaged; insertion sort sees one linear pass. Naive last-pivot Lomuto receives the worst element as every pivot, so its comparison count is quadratic. Revised hardened sort has a depth-limited heap fallback.

C4 is exactly reversed. Insertion sort has every pair inverted; naive quick sort is also quadratic but moves less. Median-of-three plus three-way partitioning should remain n log n. Revised hardened sort has a depth-limited heap fallback.

C5 has only 1% relocation, so insertion sort is cheap at small n but its inversion count grows with n. Last-pivot Lomuto is still fragile; three-way partitioning is the safer large-n choice. Revised hardened sort has a depth-limited heap fallback.

Only ~7 band values occur, creating large equal groups. Three-way partitioning groups equal bands in one pass; Lomuto degrades and also gives unstable tie order (the documented C6 conflict). Revised hardened sort has a depth-limited heap fallback.
